title: Real Prosperity
text:
A rich man came to the Zen master Sengai and asked him to write something that would bring continued prosperity to his family. He wanted a blessing that the family could treasure from one generation to the next.

Sengai took a large sheet of paper and wrote: "Father dies, son dies, grandson dies."

The rich man was furious. "I asked you to write something for the happiness of my family," he said. "Why do you make a joke of it?"

"I am not joking," Sengai answered. "If your son were to die before you, it would grieve you greatly. If your grandson died before your son, both of you would be heartbroken. If your family, generation after generation, passes away in the order I have written, it will be the natural course of life. I call that real prosperity."
lesson: The deepest good fortune a family can have is ordinary: that the old go before the young. Ordinary life in its natural order is worth being grateful for.
source: Nyogen Senzaki and Paul Reps, 101 Zen Stories (1919), Real Prosperity
